title: Ingénieur d'études (F/H)
company: Institut du Cerveau – Paris Brain Institute
description:
CONTEXTE
L’activité s’exerce au sein d’un laboratoire de recherche INSERM dont les thématiques de recherche sont centrées sur l’exploration des gènes et des mécanismes de plusieurs maladies humaines génétiques donnant des accidents vasculaires cérébraux chez l’adulte et chez l’enfant.
Les thématiques de recherche de notre groupe au sein de l’équipe GenoVASC (unité INSERM U1127, Paris Brain Institute) sont centrées sur l’exploration des mécanismes de plusieurs maladies génétiques humaines conduisant à la survenue d’accidents cérébraux chez l’enfant et chez l’adulte. Après identification des gènes causaux par des approches de génomique, des approches cellulaires et moléculaires seront utilisées pour explorer les conséquences des variants candidats identifiés.
MISSIONS PRINCIPALES
Rattaché à la chef d’équipe, l’ingénieur d’études sera chargé des missions suivantes :
Réaliser, à partir de protocoles définis, la caractérisation moléculaire et fonctionnelle de variants candidats dans une maladie génétique cérébrovasculaire, incluant :
o la culture de fibroblastes issus de sujets contrôles et de patients mutés,
o l’introduction de variants nucléotidiques dans un plasmide
o la transfection de plasmides sauvages et mutés, digestion enzymatique de ces plasmides
o la préparation d’ADN, ARN, cDNA et lysats protéiques, ainsi que leurs dosages
o le séquençage ADN et cDNA par la méthode de Sanger
o l’analyse quantitative des transcrits par amplification PCR en temps réel,
o l’analyse par western blot des protéines sauvage et mutée
Proposer et développer de nouvelles options techniques pour améliorer les protocoles, le cas échéant former l’équipe sur ces nouveaux protocoles
Tenir un cahier d’expériences, rassembler les résultats, les mettre en forme et en rendre compte
Rédiger des rapports d’expériences, des notes techniques, et actualiser le dossier de protocoles techniques
Consulter et exploiter la documentation technique, y proposer des améliorations
Assurer une veille scientifique sur les variants candidats dans les maladies génétiques cérébrovasculaires
Appliquer, en situation de travail, les règles d’hygiène et de sécurité et celles spécifiques à la manipulation de certains produits
CONDITIONS PARTICULIERES
Salaire : Entre 2 494,3€ et 2 651,49€ bruts par mois, selon profil
Durée du contrat : jusqu'à la fin de l'année, puis renouvelable jusqu'à 18 mois
Déplacements très ponctuels sur l’hôpital Bichat (service de génétique)
Contrat INSERM
PROFIL
· BAC+5 en biologie cellulaire ou moléculaire
· Une première expérience est indispensable, incluant un stage
Savoir-faire
· Maîtriser dans le cadre d’une utilisation de routine une ou plusieurs techniques d’un domaine expérimental de la biologie
· Maîtriser les outils bioinformatiques utilisés couramment en biologie moléculaire (design de primers, recherche et alignement de séquences)
· Savoir utiliser les logiciels liés aux techniques expérimentales et à la présentation des résultats
Savoir
· Connaître les bases de la biologie moléculaire et de la génétique
· Avoir une connaissance opérationnelle des appareillages utilisés (thermocycleur, thermocycleur en temps réel, appareillages d’electrophorèse sur gel et révélation…) et des techniques qu’ils requièrent
· Connaître les risques chimiques et biologiques liés aux produits, les matériels et techniques utilisés ainsi que la réglementation concernant les produits à risques (isotopes, OGM…)
Savoir-être
· Planifier, prioriser en tenant compte des objectifs fixés
· Interagir avec l’ensemble des membres de l’équipe et les autres interlocuteurs à l’ICM (notamment sur les plateformes)
· Réaliser les tâches avec rigueur
· Avoir un sens de l’organisation
· Faire preuve de curiosité et de persévérance
· Être capable gagner en autonomie rapidement
L’Institut du cerveau s’engage pour lutter contre toute forme de discrimination. Nous garantissons un environnement de travail inclusif et respectueux de toutes les diversités.
Tous nos postes sont ouverts aux personnes en situation de handicap.
Postulez directement sur notre site carrière : envoyez votre CV et lettre de motivation dans un même document pdf : https://offres.institutducerveau-icm.org/fr/jobs/2002-02

title: Scientist II, Protein Engineering
description:
Work Schedule
Standard (Mon-Fri)
Environmental Conditions
Laboratory Setting
As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer.
DESCRIPTION:
We are seeking a Scientist II with a strong background in protein engineering and relevant experience in an R&D environment. As part of the Ligand Discovery department, you will join a multidisciplinary team developing next-generation antibody-based affinity ligands for the purification of biologics.
In this role, you will apply your expertise in protein engineering, molecular biology and biochemistry to develop and characterize antibody fragments with defined binding properties. Working closely with colleagues across R&D, you will design, execute and interpret experiments that contribute to the development of innovative affinity ligands.
In addition, you will take ownership of defined scientific workstreams, identify technical challenges, propose practical solutions, and contribute to project discussions and scientific decision-making. You will contribute to the development of new products from early discovery through development while working in a collaborative and innovative environment.
What you will do:
Design, plan and execute protein-engineering experiments to improve the performance of affinity ligands.
Apply computational protein engineering, structural modeling, bioinformatics, and AI-enabled software tools to support ligand design and optimization.
Screen and characterize antibody fragments using protein-display technologies such as phage display or yeast display.
Analyze and integrate large experimental, sequence, and screening datasets to identify trends, generate actionable insights, and guide iterative engineering cycles
Contribute to project planning, coordinate experimental activities, and track progress within assigned workstreams.
Collaborate closely with multidisciplinary teams across R&D.
Share knowledge and support colleagues and junior team members where appropriate.
Stay informed about scientific and technological developments and evaluate new approaches that can strengthen our antibody-engineering platform.
REQUIREMENTS:
Minimum Requirements / Qualifications:
MSc or PhD in Molecular Biology, Biochemistry or a related life-sciences discipline. BSc candidates with extensive experience in antibody engineering may also be considered.
Relevant experience in protein engineering, preferably within the biotechnology industry or applied academic research.
Experience independently planning, executing and interpreting scientific experiments.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to laboratory safety protocols
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a proactive, hands-on approach.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across multidisciplinary teams.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
Working knowledge of Dutch is considered an advantage.
Required Technical Experience:
Protein engineering, preferably in combination with display technologies.
Molecular cloning and protein expression in microbial expression systems.
Proficiency with data analysis software and statistical tools
Immunological assays, such as ELISA.
Preferred Technical Experience:
Experience with antibodies or antibody fragments.
Experience with SPR or BLI for the analysis of protein-protein interactions.
Experience with with automated liquid handling systems and high-throughput workflows.
Experience with protein purification using FPLC.

title: Applied AI Scientist
description:
About AQEMIA
AQEMIA is a drug invention company dedicated to creating entirely new medicines to address major unmet medical needs.
At the core of our mission is
QEMI
, our proprietary molecule-invention platform, which uniquely combines cutting-edge science with advanced technology. Powered by physics-based modeling, statistical mechanics, and generative AI, QEMI allows our teams to design novel drug candidates from first principles.
What makes AQEMIA different is our commitment to true innovation: our research is dedicated to the invention of new molecular entities, not the refinement of existing ones. We focus on inventing
never-before-seen molecules
, without relying on experimental data, and advancing them into a growing pipeline of proprietary programs and strategic partnerships with leading pharmaceutical companies.
Our most advanced preclinical programs are currently
in vivo optimization
, targeting diseases still waiting for effective treatments, offering our teams the opportunity to work on science that can make a real difference in people’s lives.
For more information, visit AQEMIA.com, our WTTJ Page, and our LinkedIn.
About Our Team
AQEMIA brings together a diverse, multidisciplinary team of 80+ professionals based in Paris and London. Our scientists and engineers, including chemists, physicists, machine learning experts, and software engineers, work side by side to push the boundaries of early-stage drug discovery.
This close collaboration across disciplines is central to our approach, enabling us to tackle complex scientific challenges from first principles and translate cutting-edge ideas into novel therapeutic candidates. At AQEMIA, team members are encouraged to contribute their expertise, learn from one another, and play an active role in shaping the future of drug invention.
About Our Platform Department
The Platform team (:20 people) brings together multidisciplinary teams working on the scientific core of Aqemia’s drug discovery engine. Its mission is to build scalable and reproducible workflows enabling multiple drug discovery programs to run in parallel with minimal manual intervention.
The team combines expertise across Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (both research and applications), data science, statistical physics and molecular simulations, computational chemistry (CADD), and other scientific disciplines. Together, they develop predictive models, physics-based simulations, and robust scientific pipelines that power AQEMIA's discovery platform.
At the center of this ecosystem is the “Rocket Launcher” process: an industrialized workflow continuously launching, testing, and improving drug discovery projects through iterative scientific feedback loops.
The role
We are looking for an Applied AI Research Scientist to join Aqemia’s Drug Discovery Platform, working at the intersection of ML and molecular science. You’ll split your time between:
50% Applied AI:
Contribute directly to internal and partnered drug discovery programs by applying ML rigorously and efficiently in collaboration with chemists and project teams.
50% AI Research:
Develop cutting-edge ML models (e.g., GNNs, generative models, physics-informed AI) to predict molecular properties and protein-ligand interactions.
Responsibilities:
Applied ML for Discovery Programs (50%)
Own ML workstreams: define goals, manage timelines, communicate with stakeholders
Process molecular datasets and apply robust ML models (QSAR, regression, ranking)
Collaborate with chemists and project leads; deliver results that drive compound prioritisation
Make your models and predictions easily accessible to end users ensuring practical usability in drug discovery workflows
AI Research & Development (50%)
Design and implement novel ML algorithms (DL, GNNs, generative, physics-based models)
Take part in cutting-edge research and bibliographic exploration
Collaborate with research and drug discovery teams to translate models into actionable insights
Requirements:
Strong problem-solving skills, autonomy and a collaborative mindset
MSc or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Maths, Physics, or related field
:3-5 years of experience applying ML in scientific or industrial settings
Strong experience with ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, Scikit-learn)
Solid Python programming skills and experience working with scientific computing libraries
Nice-to-Haves
Experience with bio/health data
Preferred Mindset
Pragmatic and Impact-Driven - Focused on delivering solutions that work in real-world applications, balancing scientific rigor with practical usability
Eagerness to Learn - A strong curiosity for scientific advancements and a willingness to continuously expand your expertise
Love for High Scientific Challenges - Enthusiasm for tackling complex problems at the frontier of AI and drug discovery
Team-Oriented - A collaborative spirit, thriving in an interdisciplinary environment
Humility - Open to feedback and different perspectives, always striving for improvement
Please note that applications for this role will close on July 15, 2026.
Why Join Us?
At AQEMIA, we work for a mission: joining us means having your own impact on changing the way drugs are discovered, and helping to shape the direction of our fast-growing company and team.
Expanding Drug Discovery Pipeline
: Focused on critical therapeutic areas like Oncology, CNS, Immuno-inflammation... with in vivo proof of concept/patent stage programs. Collaborations with top Pharma, including a $140M Sanofi deal.
World-Class Interdisciplinary Team
: work alongside exceptional talent at the intersection of technology and life sciences. Our teams combine deep expertise in AI, physics-based modeling, biology, and medicinal chemistry to push the boundaries of innovation.
DeepTech Recognition
: AQEMIA is proud to be part of the
French Tech 120
and
France 2030
, highlighting our role as a key player in Europe’s DeepTech ecosystem.
Prime Location with Flexibility
: Our offices are located in the heart of
Paris
and
London (King’s Cross)
, with flexible work arrangements including up to two remote days per week.
Strong Financial Backing
: $100M raised from leading European and International investors
We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

title: Senior Scientist (all genders) - Genomic Medicine
description:
At Bayer we’re visionaries, driven to solve the world’s toughest challenges and striving for a world where ,Health for all, Hunger for none’ is no longer a dream, but a real possibility. We’re doing it with energy, curiosity and sheer dedication, always learning from unique perspectives of those around us, expanding our thinking, growing our capabilities and redefining ‘impossible’. There are so many reasons to join us. If you’re hungry to build a varied and meaningful career in a community of brilliant and diverse minds to make a real difference, there’s only one choice.
Senior Scientist (all genders) - Genomic Medicine
Are you eager to actively shape the development of innovative therapeutic programs? In this three year fixed term position, you work at the interface of science, strategy, and collaboration, closely partnering with cross functional teams and external companies. You drive projects along the entire drug discovery value chain — from target validation to the identification of preclinical candidates — taking ownership, contributing your scientific expertise, and ensuring that critical go/no go decisions are made swiftly and effectively.
Your Tasks And Responsibilities
You facilitate or co-lead the development of therapeutic programmes in cross-functional teams, including close collaboration with partner companies
You initiate and support therapeutic programmes together with key stakeholders, driving rapid and evidence-based go/no-go decisions within project teams
You lead or co-lead therapeutic research programmes through preD1, D1 and D2 stages
You support and co-lead cross-functional research teams to accelerate target identification and screening activities
You work across DDS biology subclusters and in cross-functional teams to select, design, and deliver high-quality compounds along the drug discovery value chain, from target validation to the identification of a preclinical candidate
You plan and execute research projects in matrixed, cross-functional teams to advance therapeutic hypotheses
As a scientific point of contact within project teams, you provide guidance on modality choice, lead finding strategy, and mode of action identification
You assess and prepare reports and insights on the feasibility of therapeutic strategies across therapeutic areas, enabling aligned and data-driven go/no-go decisions
You take ownership and accountability for driving projects with urgency toward key inflection points
You evaluate CROs and internal capabilities to enable project teams to make informed, project-specific decisions
In matrixed, cross-functional teams, you coordinate research assistants and foster strong collaboration across functions
You facilitate ideation and drive the pursuit of therapeutic programmes with internal and external collaborators, including arm’s length partner companies
You contribute to self-empowered matrix teams in line with Bayer’s VACC leadership principles by enabling, empowering, and supporting colleagues in a high-performance environment with a strong culture of psychological safety
You foster a culture of ownership in support of the overall strategy, promoting peer accountability across portfolio deliverables and beyond
You have the opportunity to lead or co-lead strategic initiatives and present scientific insights to senior management and key stakeholders
Who You Are
You hold a PhD in biochemistry, biology, biotechnology, pharmacy, or a related field

title: Doktorand inom multiomik, maskininlärning och cancerbioinformatik
description:

Forskarutbildningsämne: BIO Biotechnology – Cancer bioinformatik

Projektet passar särskilt bra för kandidater med bakgrund inom maskinlärning, bioinformatik, speciellt med utbildning och erfarenhet av att jobba med cancerrelevanta data och cancerbiologi.

fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå, eller
på något annat sätt inom eller utom landet förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper.
starka kunskaper inom cancerbiologi, särskilt tumörfrämjande inflammation och cancerprogression.
masterexamen inom bioinformatik, beräkningsbiologi eller relaterade cancer områden.

förmåga att arbeta självständigt och i en samarbetsinriktad teammiljö.

två akademiska eller forskningsrelaterade referenser krävs, varav minst en ska vara en chefsreferens.

erfarenhet av tvärvetenskaplig forskning och ett intresse för att samarbeta med forskare från olika områden.
god förståelse för vetenskaplig litteratur och förmåga att förstå och analysera komplex information.

en solid cancerforskning är att föredra.
